title: ClauseTree
description: Normalized clause tree for one version of one document (intermediate artifact, not OPF).

version.description: Version label within the document folder.

source_file.description: Original filename (basename) of the source document.

nodes.description: Top-level clause nodes in document order.

heading.description: Section title, or null if absent.

text.description: Body text of this node (not including children).

char_span.description: Exclusive-end character span [start, end] in the document's full normalized text, covering the whole clause: from the start of its heading line through the end of its own body text (children excluded). OPF citations' char_span use this span.

heading_span.description: Exclusive-end character span [start, end] of the heading line alone, in the same coordinate system as char_span. Absent or null when the node has no separate heading line (the synthetic pre-heading '0' node, sub-clauses promoted from body text, LLM/agent-grounded nodes). When present, heading_span[0] == char_span[0] and heading_span[1] <= char_span[1].

page.description: 1-based source page the clause begins on, or null when unpaginated or unknown.

x_resegmented.description: Vendor key (issue #255). Present on a node the re-segmentation pass split out of, or joined from, other nodes: {split_from | joined_with, basis, origin_span / origin_spans, scores, to / at}. char_span of such a node lies inside the original node's span (or covers the two joined spans), so an OPF citation still resolves to the original bytes. A node split out of another is numbered '<clause_path>.r<k>' and is a child of the node it was cut from. A node the agent sub-split made (issue #257) records {subsplit_from, basis: 'agent', origin_span, span, of, key}; its later spans are numbered '<clause_path>.s<k>'.

x_non_clause.description: Vendor key (issue #255). Present on an unclassified node that is not a clause (numbering_only, signature_block, heading_or_placeholder, header_footer, fragment, lead_in, ocr_junk, email). The node is kept so citations resolve; it is left out of classification, precedent and absence counts.
